about: Who is speaking, for reading the dialogues aloud (milestone 14): each person keeps one voice in every dialogue. The speakers are those named in the Perseus markup of the Loeb English (build_db.py, speaker_names), one name per person. This file says only where the markup's names and the persons differ, and quotes the Loeb English for each; every other name is its own person, in every dialogue where it appears (Socrates, Alcibiades, the Athenian of the Laws and the Epinomis). Joint speakers ('Lysis #Menexenus') are read as one voice for the pair.

persons.why: The narrator of the Parmenides is named in both spellings in the markup; he is addressed as Cephalus and comes from Clazomenae.

evidence.quote: When we came from our home at Clazomenae to Athens

persons.why: The Cretan of the Laws, spelled Clinias there and Cleinias in the Epinomis, where the same three meet again.

evidence.quote: We Cretans call Zeus our lawgiver
we have come all three—you and I and Megillus here

persons.why: The youth of the Euthydemus is another man than the Cretan of the Laws.

evidence.quote: He is the son of Axiochus

anonymous_about: Names that stand for an unnamed person (the Friend of the Hipparchus and of the Protagoras, the Companion of the Minos and of the Symposium): one voice in each dialogue, not shared between dialogues.
